squawks.headline: US UMich sentiment rises to 51 in preliminary reading against a 48 forecast; 1-year inflation expectations ease to 4.3%
squawks.detail: The University of Michigan preliminary sentiment index came in at 51 against a 48 forecast and 48.0 previously; current conditions were 51 (forecast 47, previous 46.7) and expectations 50.9 (forecast 49, previous 48.8). One-year inflation expectations fell to 4.3% from 4.7% (forecast 4.6%), and five-year expectations fell to 3.4% from 3.5% (forecast 3.5%).

squawks.headline: Fed's Musalem says clear Fed communication helps policy pass through to the economy more smoothly
squawks.detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said that good communication from the Fed leads to smoother transmission of monetary policy. The remark was part of his comments on Friday.

squawks.headline: White House adviser Hassett says inflation is falling and he sees no policy change that needs planning
squawks.detail: The National Economic Council's Hassett said the data show strong growth and slowing inflation, that the administration's policies are working, and that the job market is firing on all cylinders.

squawks.headline: Fed's Musalem says excess US inflation comes from both supply and demand; expects AI to lift productivity sharply
squawks.detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said the data centre build-out is adding to strong demand and that AI will bring much higher productivity.

squawks.headline: White House adviser Hassett says Trump will decide on Fed Governor Cook after reading the report
squawks.detail: Senior White House adviser Hassett also said headline inflation is being driven by energy and Iran, and that he sees no need to plan a policy change.

squawks.headline: Fed's Musalem blames excess US inflation on energy shocks and the AI build-out; says consumption and investment are growing fast
squawks.detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said inflation must come back to 2% in a timely way. He said data-centre construction is adding to strong demand and that AI will bring much higher productivity.

squawks.headline: Fed's Musalem says public concern about current inflation persists but expectations remain anchored
squawks.detail: St Louis Fed President Musalem said people are still worried about inflation at its present level. He also said inflation expectations remain anchored.

squawks.headline: Iranian source says Tehran is responding positively to the latest proposal from mediators
squawks.detail: An Iranian source told Al Arabiya that Tehran is responding positively to the newest proposal put forward by mediators in the US-Iran talks. Separately, a senior Iranian security official repeated that Tehran wants concrete US action before a new phase of diplomacy.

squawks.headline: White House adviser Hassett points to three months of strong US job growth and says inflation should be slowing
squawks.detail: In a CNBC interview, White House senior adviser Kevin Hassett said he was looking at the last three months of very strong job growth and, when asked about the Fed, said inflation should be slowing. He also said an AI bubble is a fair concern, but the US economy could still be very strong even if data centre building slows.

squawks.headline: ECB considers reviewing bank lending to data centres
squawks.detail: The ECB is weighing a review of bank loans to data centres, according to a market news post on Friday afternoon. No timing or scope was given.

squawks.headline: Bank of Canada December hike odds fall to about 32% from 40% after weak jobs report, swaps show
squawks.detail: Swaps pricing shows the market-implied chance of a December Bank of Canada rate hike fell to roughly 32% from 40% after Canada's October jobs data.

squawks.headline: US 2-year Treasury yield rises 4bp after October payrolls beat forecasts
squawks.detail: An economist reported the US 2-year yield up 4bp after the payrolls release came in above forecasts. The rise came as the sell-off in AI and tech stocks continued.

squawks.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield rises 6.3bp to 4.898% after jobs data as traders add to December Fed hike bets
squawks.detail: US Treasury yields extended gains after the October employment report, with the 10-year yield last up 6.3bp at 4.898%. Traders were reported to be adding to bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike in December.

squawks.headline: US payrolls rise 165K in October against a 70K forecast; unemployment rate falls to 4.1%
squawks.detail: US October nonfarm payrolls rose 165,000 against a 70,000 forecast, after 29,000 the previous month, and two-month revisions added 84,000. The unemployment rate was 4.1% against a 4.2% forecast, and average hourly earnings rose 0.4% m/m and 3.1% y/y, against forecasts of 0.3% and 2.9%.

squawks.headline: Canada loses 4.7K jobs in October against a forecast 15K gain; unemployment rate rises to 6.7%
squawks.detail: Canadian employment fell by 4,700 in October against a forecast rise of 15,000, after a 68,300 fall the previous month. The unemployment rate rose to 6.7% from 6.5%, and average hourly earnings growth slowed to 2% y/y from 2.30%, against a 2.05% forecast.

squawks.headline: FTSE 100 drops 2% and heads for its steepest fall in more than seven months as AI worries drive a global sell-off
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that the FTSE 100 fell 2% on Friday and was on course for a weekly decline. It links the global sell-off to jitters over AI that followed the change in the US political landscape.

squawks.headline: UK PM Burnham rules out crude spending cuts and says he will not chase numbers
squawks.detail: Prime Minister Burnham said the government would not pursue crude spending cuts or chase numbers. He spoke after earlier saying he was ready to take difficult decisions on benefits.

squawks.headline: UK PM Burnham says he is ready to take difficult decisions on benefits
squawks.detail: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he is prepared to make tough choices on benefits spending, according to a report on Friday. No specific measures or figures were given.

squawks.headline: BoE's Pill says margins and wage setting show no evidence of second-round effects
squawks.detail: Bank of England chief economist Huw Pill said there is no evidence of second-round effects in firms' margins or in wage setting.

squawks.headline: BoE's Pill says the Bank is giving weight to pay bargaining, costs and pricing
squawks.detail: Bank of England Chief Economist Huw Pill said the MPC is weighing pay settlements, cost pressures and firms' pricing behaviour. He made the remarks in the same appearance in which he said rates could be held or cut if growth stalls.

squawks.headline: BoE's Pill says a decision on a second hike will be made in the coming weeks and the rate path from spring will depend on data
squawks.detail: BoE Chief Economist Huw Pill said there is not yet enough evidence of second-round effects, energy prices are still building pressure in the pipeline, and evidence on second-round effects will come through from spring. He also said the MPC's camps differed in emphasis on the decision and called AI-driven growth somewhat encouraging.

squawks.headline: BoE's Pill says nothing is baked in for rates next year and Bank Rate could hold or even fall if growth stalls
squawks.detail: Bank of England Chief Economist Huw Pill said the outlook becomes more uncertain from the spring and that Bank Rate could stay on hold or fall if growth stalls next year. He named the squeeze on company margins, and how firms respond to it, as the key factor.

squawks.headline: BoE's Pill calls the rate hike pre-emptive and says the Bank will not repeat the 2022 hiking cycle
squawks.detail: BoE Chief Economist Huw Pill said there is not yet evidence of second-round effects, but energy prices are creating pipeline pressure and activity and employment are adding to demand at the margin. He also said MPC members took different views and stressed different points around the decision.

squawks.headline: US and Iran move closer to a possible deal to end the war, Bloomberg reports, with Tehran open to nuclear topics once ruled out
squawks.detail: Bloomberg reports that the US and Iran are nearing a possible agreement to end the war. It says Tehran is willing to discuss nuclear issues it had previously treated as off-limits.

squawks.headline: Senior Iranian official says written US commitments on a deal are not enough and Tehran wants action before talks begin
squawks.detail: According to reports, a senior Iranian official said Iran will not start negotiations until Washington takes practical steps, and that written American commitments on the agreement do not satisfy Tehran.

squawks.headline: UK Budget keeps the Local Housing Allowance freeze in place into 2027-28, Resolution Foundation says
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation says keeping the LHA freeze into 2027-28 leaves more than a million families worse off, 91% of them in the bottom half of the income distribution. It also notes that the Budget's Your First Home scheme will help a small number of renters to buy.

squawks.headline: Spain puts forward former Bank of Spain governor Pablo Hernández de Cos as its candidate for ECB president
squawks.detail: Spain's deputy prime minister announced the nomination in a letter to the Eurogroup president.

squawks.headline: Belgian King rejects PM De Wever's resignation and tells him to restart budget negotiations at once
squawks.detail: The Belgian royal palace says the King met Prime Minister Bart De Wever and the heads of the five majority parties, then declined to accept the prime minister's resignation. He asked him to resume budget negotiations immediately to resolve the crisis.

squawks.headline: Iran says diplomacy with the US can only progress if Washington takes practical steps, state broadcaster reports
squawks.detail: Iranian state broadcaster IRIB reported that Tehran wants practical steps from the US before diplomacy between the two moves forward. The report comes as mediators led by Qatar try to broker an interim US-Iran deal.

squawks.headline: Shriti Vadera becomes external adviser to UK finance minister Healey, focusing on delivery of the UK G20
squawks.detail: A market newswire reports that Shriti Vadera has been named an external adviser to UK finance minister Healey. Her role covers delivery of the UK G20.

squawks.headline: Eurozone retail sales fall 0.7% m/m, missing the -0.1% forecast; annual growth slows to 0.4%
squawks.detail: Eurozone retail sales fell 0.7% month on month against a forecast of -0.1% and a previous 0.1%. Year-on-year growth was 0.4%, below the 0.6% forecast and down from 0.8% previously.

squawks.headline: EU Council agrees position to delay EU methane rules by one year to 1 January 2028
squawks.detail: The Irish presidency says the Council of the EU has agreed to push the start of the EU methane regulation back to 1 January 2028. A document seen by Reuters shows the position allows further one-year postponements if implementation is not ready.

squawks.headline: ECB's Lane says inflation must return to target within one to two years and financial conditions have tightened
squawks.detail: ECB chief economist Lane said monetary policy's role is to contain spillover effects and that data should be gathered until December before any decision. He also said strong exports are giving the economy a boost.

squawks.headline: Fed's Williams says US inflation has been too high for too long and must return to 2% promptly; sees tariff effects mostly past
squawks.detail: New York Fed President Williams said growth has improved, the labour market is strong, inflation expectations are stable and wage growth is consistent with the target. He also said monetary policy takes 1-2 years to have its effect and AI has had a limited impact on prices.

squawks.headline: ECB's Lane says energy inflation will feed into wage talks and price setting; expects fiscal tightening next year
squawks.detail: ECB chief economist Philip Lane said energy inflation would shape wage negotiations and price setting across the economy. He also said fiscal policy has been looser than expected, but the ECB expects it to tighten next year and beyond.

squawks.headline: Fed's Williams calls the US economy remarkably resilient and says it is an appropriate time to gather more information
squawks.detail: New York Fed President Williams said growth has strengthened, the labour market is stable and solid, and the effects of tariffs are mostly behind them. He said energy is feeding through to inflation as expected, inflation expectations are well anchored and wage growth is consistent with the 2% goal.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says European security needs discussing in a Ukraine settlement but Europe cannot agree on its representatives
squawks.detail: The Kremlin also praised recent meetings at the White House and said there is willingness to continue humanitarian work after the evacuation from Oleshky.

squawks.headline: Swiss consumer confidence falls to -44.9, well below the -35.5 forecast
squawks.detail: The seasonally adjusted Swiss consumer confidence index came in at -44.9, against a forecast of -35.5 and a previous reading of -34.

squawks.headline: BoE's Bailey says another rate hike is possible if energy prices stay high
squawks.detail: BoE Governor Andrew Bailey said a further rate rise could come if energy prices remain elevated, and that private-sector wage growth is at the upper end of the range consistent with the inflation target. In the same remarks he said the Bank is firmly on top of cyber risks and that recent hacks show the need to understand frontier AI models well.

squawks.headline: BoE's Bailey says he does not accept that UK inflation has become endemic
squawks.detail: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said he disagrees that the UK has endemic inflation. The remark follows the Bank's first rate hike in more than three years.

squawks.headline: Oil falls back below $100 a barrel as the global tech sell-off deepens
squawks.detail: City AM reports oil trading below $100 early on Friday, with the FTSE 100 expected to open sharply lower after South Korea's Kospi fell more than 5% and trading on the exchange was halted. Reuters also reports an oil slide on Friday.

squawks.headline: Qatar's Emir and Trump hold talks on efforts to de-escalate the Middle East conflict
squawks.detail: Qatar's Emir and US President Trump discussed efforts to de-escalate in the Middle East, according to reports on Friday morning. Qatar is leading mediation towards an interim US-Iran deal.

squawks.headline: UK house prices fall 1.2% year on year in October, Lloyds says, with the average price at £296,285
squawks.detail: Lloyds puts the average UK house price in October at £296,285, the same as its September figure, and prices were down 1.2% on a year earlier. The lender says a difficult economic backdrop is testing housing demand.

squawks.headline: German September industrial production rises 0.7% m/m, beating the -0.1% forecast; annual growth slows to 0.4%
squawks.detail: German industrial production rose 0.7% month on month in September against a forecast of -0.1%, after 2.0% the month before. Year on year, output grew 0.4% against a 1.2% forecast, down from 2.3% previously.

squawks.headline: Shanghai crude front-month futures rise 2.00% intraday to 651.20 yuan a barrel
squawks.detail: China's Shanghai crude (SC) front-month contract rose 2.00% during the session to 651.20 yuan a barrel, according to a market commentary account.

squawks.headline: Qatar-led mediators step up efforts to broker an interim US-Iran deal to end the war, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that regional negotiators led by Qatar are pushing harder for an interim agreement between Washington and Tehran. It also reports that Iran is celebrating the Republicans' midterm defeat.

squawks.headline: EU-China trade truce comes under threat as both sides prepare for possible escalation, SCMP reports
squawks.detail: The South China Morning Post reports that the EU and China are each getting ready for the trade dispute to escalate, which puts their truce at risk.

squawks.headline: Brent crude futures climb more than $2 and break above $100 a barrel
squawks.detail: Brent futures rose by more than $2 in Asian trading to go above $100 a barrel. US crude futures earlier gained $1 to $91.52 a barrel.

squawks.headline: South Korea's finance minister pledges proactive steps to calm markets, including easing rules on borrowed investment
squawks.detail: South Korea's finance minister said the stock market is overreacting to external factors and that further stabilising measures will follow if volatility rises. The KOSPI fell below 5,000 during the Asian tech sell-off, Yonhap reported.

squawks.headline: US Democrats are drawing up a plan to reverse Trump's tariffs on Canada, WSJ reports
squawks.detail: The Wall Street Journal reported the plan after Democrats' midterm election gains.

squawks.headline: Japan's PM Takaichi wants proceeds from the BoJ's faster ETF sales to fund spending on economic security
squawks.detail: Takaichi said the proceeds could cover bond payments, allowing the government to fund public investment. In the same remarks she said she is watching the global market turbulence closely and that it is unclear whether the falls in AI and chip shares will be temporary.

squawks.headline: Japan's 2-year yield falls 6bp to 1.795% and China's 10-year yield hits a record low as the Asian tech sell-off deepens
squawks.detail: The 2-year JGB yield fell 6bp to 1.795% and China's 10-year yield fell to a record low. South Korea's KOSPI dropped more than 8%, which set off a 20-minute trading halt, and the Nikkei was down 6.72%, 20% below its June peak.

squawks.headline: 10-year JGB futures rise 0.9 point in early trade as Nikkei futures fall 7%
squawks.detail: Benchmark 10-year Japanese government bond futures gained 0.9 point in early Tokyo trade while Nikkei average futures fell 7%. South Korea's KOSPI dropped 8.8%, triggering a circuit breaker that halted trading for 8 minutes.

squawks.headline: Japan's September total cash earnings rise 4.6% year on year, above the 3.8% forecast
squawks.detail: Japanese government data show September cash earnings up 4.6% year on year, against a 3.8% forecast and 3.8% previously. Real wages rose 2.2% and overtime pay rose 3.6%.

squawks.headline: Iran says its nuclear proposal to the US will be discussed only once Washington meets Tehran's seven demands
squawks.detail: A senior Iranian official told Reuters on Thursday that the proposal went to the United States via Qatar. The official said talks on it depend on the US first meeting Iran's seven demands.

squawks.headline: US envoy Kushner says the US will host the first US-Ukraine-Russia peace talks since February in Abu Dhabi next week
squawks.detail: US envoy Jared Kushner said Washington will convene the three-way talks with Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi next week. They would be the first such trilateral talks since February.

squawks.headline: US Treasury yields fall 6bp to 4.83% as a tech stock rout drives a flight to safety
squawks.detail: Treasury yields fell six basis points to 4.83% as selling spread to other markets after the Nasdaq 100 dropped 6.4% and the S&P 500 fell 4.4%. The selloff was linked to fears of AI regulation, slower data-centre investment and weak outlooks from Qualcomm and Arm.

squawks.headline: Trump says he met Putin envoy Dmitriev and a Russia-Ukraine settlement is very close, in a deal involving all of Europe
squawks.detail: US President Trump said he met Russia's Dmitriev on Thursday and that the US is very close to settling the Russia-Ukraine war. He said the deal would be a big agreement involving all of Europe.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US must choose between going further on Iran and certifying the current position
squawks.detail: US President Trump made the remarks on Thursday evening about Iran. The post did not say exactly what would be certified, and no market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Trump says Iran is doing nothing without US approval and says he will take many actions over the next couple of weeks
squawks.detail: US President Trump made the remarks on Thursday evening while asked about Iran. He gave no details of what the actions would be.

squawks.headline: Canada plans C$611bn of borrowing in 2027/28, including C$316bn in bonds, and lowers its GDP growth forecasts
squawks.detail: Canada's 2026 budget puts 2027/28 borrowing at C$611bn, up from C$587bn in 2026/27, with C$316bn in bond issuance, C$290bn in Treasury bills and 72% going to refinance maturing debt. It projects a 2027/28 deficit of C$62.5bn, has debt-to-GDP peaking at 40.4% in 2028/29, and cuts growth forecasts to 1.0% for 2026 and 1.7% for 2027.

squawks.headline: Canada projects a C$62.3bn federal deficit for 2026-27
squawks.detail: Canada's federal deficit is projected at C$62.3bn for the 2026-27 fiscal year, according to a market newswire report.

squawks.headline: China urges the US and EU to reconsider tariffs on Chinese goods as its exports hit record highs
squawks.detail: Beijing said it would buy more US farm goods, but only if both sides agreed to make deep cuts to tariffs, Semafor reports.

squawks.headline: Brent crude futures settle 3.88% higher at $98.29 a barrel
squawks.detail: Brent futures settled up $3.67 at $98.29 a barrel on Thursday, a 3.88% gain on the day.

squawks.headline: Iran says it has sent the US a nuclear proposal via Qatar, which the US is now reviewing
squawks.detail: A senior Iranian official said the proposal was passed on through Qatar and will be discussed only once the US meets Iran's seven demands. The official added that Washington is reviewing it.

squawks.headline: Trump blames the Republican midterm defeat on the Iran war but says he would make the same decision again
squawks.detail: Semafor reports that President Trump blamed the Republicans' midterm losses on the Iran war while saying he would do it again. Semafor also reports that traders saw the Democrats' wins as lowering the risk of escalation between Washington and Tehran.

squawks.headline: WTI crude December futures settle 2.72% higher at $90.52 a barrel
squawks.detail: NYMEX WTI December futures rose $2.40 to settle at $90.52 a barrel. NYMEX December diesel settled at $4.3519 a gallon and gasoline at $2.7634 a gallon.

squawks.headline: Saudi Aramco cuts its December Arab Light official selling price for Asia to -$7/bbl
squawks.detail: Saudi Aramco has lowered the December official selling price for Arab Light crude to Asian buyers to -$7/bbl, according to a market news post.

squawks.headline: Iran's Rezaei says Putin pledged to do whatever it takes to end the war and condemned strikes on Iran's nuclear sites
squawks.detail: Iranian reports cite Major General Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, as saying that Russia's President Putin promised to do whatever is needed to end the war. Rezaei also said Putin condemned the bombing of Iran's nuclear sites and called the war against Iran cruel.

squawks.headline: Yemen's Houthis claim an attack on King Fahd airport in Saudi Arabia's Dammam; no immediate Saudi confirmation
squawks.detail: Yemen's Houthi movement says it attacked King Fahd airport in Dammam, in Saudi Arabia. Saudi Arabia has not immediately confirmed the claim.

squawks.headline: Odds of a December Fed hike drop to 67% from above 80% as Democrats are reported to sweep Congress
squawks.detail: A market commentary account reported that, after the US midterm results, odds of a December Fed rate hike fell from above 80% to 67%. It said prediction markets now give a hold a 33% chance, the highest since mid-September.

squawks.headline: Iran is reviewing concrete proposals on its nuclear programme, officials tell the NYT
squawks.detail: The New York Times reports, citing officials, that Iran is reviewing concrete proposals on its nuclear programme. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Iran's Rezaei and Russia's Putin discuss ending the war, Al Mayadeen reports
squawks.detail: Al Mayadeen reports that ending the Iran war was the main focus of talks between Iranian official Rezaei and President Putin. Iran's position that the Strait of Hormuz stays closed until its seven conditions are met remains unchanged.

squawks.headline: Iran's Rezaei says Tehran won't reopen the Strait of Hormuz until its seven conditions are met and won't negotiate on this
squawks.detail: Rezaei said the decision on the Strait of Hormuz is not open to negotiation. An Iranian source said that ending the war is the main focus of his talks with Russian President Putin. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: BoC's Macklem hopes for lower US tariffs but says trade tensions could escalate before they improve
squawks.detail: Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem said he was optimistic that US tariffs could come down. He added that an escalation could not be ruled out before trade with the US improves.

squawks.headline: ECB's Lagarde says the secondary effects of the energy price shock need watching, with demand shocks also under way
squawks.detail: ECB President Christine Lagarde said policymakers must monitor second-round effects of the energy price shock. She added that demand shocks are happening at the same time.

squawks.headline: Putin envoy Dmitriev praises the Oleshky ceasefire and says Putin values Trump's peace efforts
squawks.detail: Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev held up the humanitarian ceasefire in Oleshky as an example of what cooperation can achieve, and said Putin appreciates Trump's peacemaking efforts. Separately, there were reports that Melania Trump said she took part in planning the Oleshky humanitarian operation.

squawks.headline: BoE's Bailey says inflation risks lie to the upside and peace moves would bring only limited relief
squawks.detail: Bank of England Governor Bailey said the Bank is monitoring how far inflation passes through, that future decisions depend on how quickly inflation falls, and that the energy price cap currently locks in some inflation. He said the upside risks to inflation could change.

squawks.headline: ECB's Lagarde says US tariffs are unlikely to be revisited soon, though the midterm vote may affect them over time
squawks.detail: ECB President Lagarde said she does not expect US tariffs to be reconsidered right away. She said the US midterm result may have an effect on tariffs but that it would take time.

squawks.headline: ECB's Lagarde says many indicators will arrive before the December meeting
squawks.detail: ECB President Lagarde said a large amount of data will come in between now and the December policy meeting. She had also described the current situation as made difficult by the energy shock and AI pulling in opposite directions.

squawks.headline: ECB's Lagarde says energy shock and AI pull in opposite directions and tools are still needed to stop inflation running away
squawks.detail: ECB President Lagarde said the current situation is complicated by the energy shock and AI pulling in opposite directions, and that separating supply-driven from demand-driven shocks is very difficult. She said it is still necessary to apply tools to prevent inflation from running away.

squawks.headline: Gilt yields rise after the BoE's first rate hike in more than three years, Reuters reports
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that gilt yields rose after the Bank of England raised rates on Thursday, its first increase in over three years. The Bank said at least one more rise was likely if the US-Iran conflict continues.

squawks.headline: Iran reports three more tankers damaged in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that Iran said three more tankers had been damaged in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday. This follows earlier Iranian state media reports of two tankers hitting sea mines east of the strait.

squawks.headline: Fed's Hammack sees the possibility that the US labour market is strengthening
squawks.detail: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said she sees the labour market potentially getting stronger. She made the remark during the same appearance in which she earlier backed gradual rate rises.

squawks.headline: Fed's Hammack says she sees inflationary pressures spreading across the US economy
squawks.detail: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said inflation pressures are spreading more widely through the economy. She made the comments in remarks on Thursday.

squawks.headline: Fed's Hammack says cutting FOMC meetings to six a year from eight would be a modest change
squawks.detail: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said reducing the number of FOMC policy meetings from eight to six a year would be a modest shift. Earlier, Richmond Fed President Barkin also said changing how often meetings are held would not be a big deal.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barkin says rate rises can weigh on demand and, over time, on oil prices
squawks.detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin made the remark near the end of a Q&A session, which has since finished.

squawks.headline: Fed's Hammack says stablecoin use by AI agents would mark a major shift
squawks.detail: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack commented on AI agents using stablecoins. Her remarks came on 5 November.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barkin says credit conditions in the banking sector look reassuring for now
squawks.detail: Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin said on Thursday that credit dynamics in the banking sector are reassuring at present.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barkin says changing how often the Fed holds policy meetings would not be a big deal
squawks.detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said a change in the number of policy-setting meetings would not matter much. He added that a different meeting pace would mean more data arriving before each meeting.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation finds three in five of the richest fifth of households qualify for the £100 Household Energy Payment
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation says the £100 Household Energy Payment announced last week is poorly targeted. It adds that one in six of the poorest families report being unable to afford to heat their homes.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barkin says the AI buildout has added to inflation in the near term
squawks.detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said the build-out of AI infrastructure has had an inflationary effect in the near term. He also said data centres lack natural local constituencies because they employ few workers.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barkin links productivity gains to adapting to post-pandemic labour shortages rather than to AI
squawks.detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said the main current driver of productivity is adaptation to the labour shortages that began during the pandemic, not AI. The remarks follow US Q3 productivity rising 3.6%.

squawks.headline: Resolution Foundation says the BoE's higher inflation forecast cuts average private-sector pay by £670 next year
squawks.detail: The Resolution Foundation said the Bank of England has raised its projected inflation peak to 4.9%. It estimates this takes £670 off the average private-sector salary next year.

squawks.headline: Fed's Barkin calls inflation the Fed's biggest risk, puts policy near neutral and says a gradual pace makes sense
squawks.detail: Richmond Fed President Barkin said he expects inflation neither to speed up nor to fall for now, and that firms see broad cost pressures, starting with tariffs over the past 18 months, which they feel they must pass on. He described demand as solid and said businesses are cautious about hiring but are not yet laying staff off, that the budget deficit is sizeable, and that the policy path is clear and the question is pace.

squawks.headline: Iranian state media says two tankers hit sea mines and caught fire east of the Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: Iran's state broadcaster IRIB said two tankers struck mines and caught fire around midday on Thursday east of the Strait of Hormuz, and reported a rise in the number of tankers on fire in the area. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Fed's Hammack says policy must move to a restrictive stance and favours gradual rate hikes to return inflation to 2%
squawks.detail: Cleveland Fed President Hammack said inflation has been too high and moving in the wrong direction, and that she prefers frequent, smaller rate moves because they disrupt the economy and financial system less. She also said Fed independence is critical to bringing inflation back to 2%, and that the dollar's reserve status depends on US institutions, the rule of law and an independent Fed.

squawks.headline: US Q3 productivity rises 3.6%, beating the 2.7% forecast, while unit labour costs fall 0.7% against a 0.4% rise expected
squawks.detail: Preliminary Q3 figures show US productivity at 3.6%, up from 1.4% previously, and unit labour costs at -0.7%, down from 1.2%. Treasury yields were reported as holding steady after the data, with the 10-year up 1.04bp at 4.902% and the 2-year up 3.31bp at 4.614%.

squawks.headline: US initial jobless claims fall to 189K in the week to 31 October, below the 196K forecast
squawks.detail: US initial claims fell by 6K to 189K, and the previous week was revised to 195K. Continuing claims for the week to 24 October rose by 23K to 1.718M, against a 1.71M forecast.

squawks.headline: Iran, Saudi and Qatari foreign ministers discuss progress in diplomatic efforts towards regional stability
squawks.detail: An Iranian statement said Iran's foreign minister spoke by phone with his Saudi and Qatari counterparts. According to the statement, they discussed the latest progress in diplomatic efforts to bring stability to the region.

squawks.headline: SNB's Schlegel says Swiss inflation is mainly confined to fuel and energy, with no sign of broader price pressures
squawks.detail: SNB Chairman Schlegel said current Swiss inflation is mostly limited to fuel and energy, and the Bank does not see price pressures broadening at present. He also said the SNB has the right tools to fight inflation in future.

squawks.headline: BoE's Bailey backs greater trade and openness with the EU and links above-target inflation to very large supply shocks
squawks.detail: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said he favours greater trade and openness when asked about closer ties with the EU. Asked about UK inflation staying above target, he said the economy has been dealing with very big supply shocks.

squawks.headline: BoE's Bailey says he hopes the Bank will know more about the war's outcome by December
squawks.detail: Bank of England Governor Bailey said he hoped more information on how the war turns out would be available by the December meeting. He spoke on the day the Bank raised Bank Rate.

squawks.headline: BoE's Lombardelli says public-sector pay is not a particular risk and the minimum wage rise is at or below expectations
squawks.detail: Bank of England Deputy Governor Lombardelli said the minimum wage increase was in line with or below expectations and that public-sector wages were not a particular risk. She added that consumer-facing firms report less pricing power than business-to-business firms. She spoke on the day of the Bank's rate decision.

squawks.headline: Banks take £142.8bn in the Bank of England's short-term repo operation
squawks.detail: Banks borrowed £142.8bn through the Bank of England's short-term repo operation on 5 November.

squawks.headline: BoE's Ramsden says the decline in UK services inflation appears to have slowed or stopped
squawks.detail: Bank of England Deputy Governor Ramsden said the downward trend in UK services price inflation looks to have slowed or halted.

squawks.headline: SNB's Schlegel says the central bank does not believe in using forward guidance
squawks.detail: Swiss National Bank Chairman Schlegel said the SNB does not favour giving forward guidance.

squawks.headline: BoE's Bailey rejects a 'two and done' rates outlook and sees a case for another 25bp hike if the war does not end
squawks.detail: Bank of England Governor Bailey said he would not commit to a two-hike path and that, without an end to the war, he can see the argument for a further 25bp rise. He added that conditions are too volatile to rely on two days of news that has not been backed by a clear move towards a peace process.

squawks.headline: BoE's Bailey says he does not believe the Bank has moved too late
squawks.detail: The Bank of England Governor made the remark after the MPC raised Bank Rate to 4.0% from 3.75%.

squawks.headline: BoE's Lombardelli says eurozone inflation data show the UK is not alone in its exposure to energy prices
squawks.detail: The Bank of England Deputy Governor made the comment after the MPC's decision to raise Bank Rate to 4.0%.

squawks.headline: Oil heads for its biggest weekly fall since the pandemic, Reuters reports
squawks.detail: Reuters says the drop follows a Democratic sweep of Congress in the US midterm elections.

squawks.headline: BoE's Bailey says the rate decision would have been the same even with knowledge of the past 48 hours' events
squawks.detail: The Bank of England Governor said news over the last 48 hours has an important bearing on the outlook, but the decision would not have changed. He added that a peace process would be welcome and would bring energy prices down.

squawks.headline: BoE's Bailey says a further rise in Bank Rate may be warranted unless there is progress towards resolving the conflict
squawks.detail: At his press conference after the hike, the Governor said market pricing for more tightening next year mostly reflects risk premia rather than expected rates, which he called a fair reflection of energy risks. He welcomed the latest fall in oil prices and said good news on the conflict would mean CPI peaking somewhat below 5%.

squawks.headline: Brent fell almost 7% on Wednesday after US Vice President Vance blamed the war for Republican midterm losses
squawks.detail: An economist reported that Brent dropped almost 7% after the Vice President's social media post, which linked the steep Republican losses at the midterms to the war.

squawks.headline: BoE's Bailey says economic activity has proved more resilient than expected and business investment has grown more than forecast
squawks.detail: The Bank of England Governor made the remarks after today's rate decision, alongside comments on limiting the impact of the Iran conflict and on high domestic inflation pressures.

squawks.headline: SNB's Schlegel says the policy rate is the main tool, with FX intervention used if necessary
squawks.detail: The Swiss National Bank chairman also said Switzerland is highly exposed to external shocks and the franc has relatively strong safe-haven properties.

squawks.headline: BoE's Bailey says domestic inflation pressures that were already present remain high
squawks.detail: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said underlying domestic inflation pressures that predate the latest shock are still elevated. He made the remarks after the MPC raised Bank Rate to 4.0%.

squawks.headline: BoE's Bailey says the impact of the Iran conflict needs to be limited
squawks.detail: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said the impact of the conflict in Iran must be contained. He spoke on the day the Bank raised Bank Rate to 4.0%.

squawks.headline: Germany's Merz warns 'Made in Europe' rules could disrupt competition and says EU trade tools must not erode competitiveness
squawks.detail: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said EU 'Made in Europe' requirements could disrupt competition, and that EU trade instruments should not weaken Europe's competitive edge. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: BoE's Taylor and Dhingra describe the rate hike as insurance against worse inflation outcomes
squawks.detail: MPC members Alan Taylor and Swati Dhingra said the increase in Bank Rate serves as insurance against inflation turning out worse, according to remarks published with the decision.

squawks.headline: BoE forecasts are conditioned on market rates implying Bank Rate of 4.9% in Q4 2027
squawks.detail: According to the Monetary Policy Report, market rates imply Bank Rate at 3.9% in Q4 2026, 4.9% in Q4 2027, 4.9% in Q4 2028 and 4.7% in Q4 2029.

squawks.headline: BoE cuts its unemployment projections and raises its private-sector wage growth path from July
squawks.detail: The Monetary Policy Report sees unemployment at 4.8% in 2026, 4.9% in 2027 and 5.1% in 2028, against 5.0%, 5.3% and 5.2% in July. Private-sector regular pay growth is seen at 3.2% y/y in Q4 2026, 3.5% in Q4 2027 and 3.4% in Q4 2028 (July: 3.0%, 3.1%, 3.1%), and real post-tax labour income growth at -0.1% in 2026, -0.6% in 2027 and 1.0% in 2028 (July: 0.1%, 0.5%, 1.1%).

squawks.headline: BoE adverse scenario has CPI inflation peaking at 6.2% in Q3 2027
squawks.detail: The adverse scenario in the Bank of England's November Monetary Policy Report shows CPI peaking at 6.2% in Q3 2027.

squawks.headline: Traders add to BoE tightening bets after the decision, pricing a 35% chance of a December hike
squawks.detail: Money markets increased bets on further Bank of England rate rises after the decision and now price a 35% probability of another hike in December.

squawks.headline: BoE Monetary Policy Report sees CPI peaking around 5% in Q2 2027 and back at 2% by Q3 2028
squawks.detail: In its central projection the Bank raises its 2027 growth forecast to 1.3% from 1.1% and expects GDP growth to fall back in the coming quarters. It estimates the Budget will lower inflation by 0.25 percentage points by Q2 2027, with that effect reversing a year later, and will lift demand by 0.1% in 2026-27 before dragging on it by a little over 0.1% by 2029-30.

squawks.headline: All nine MPC members vote to hike: eight back 25bp to 4.0%, Mann dissents in favour of a 50bp rise
squawks.detail: The Bank of England's vote was 8-1 for the move to 4.0%, with Mann preferring 50bp, against a Reuters poll forecast of 7-2. No member voted to hold or cut; the FT reports it is the first rise in borrowing costs since 2023.

squawks.headline: BoE's Lombardelli, Pill and Greene point to further rate rises; Bailey calls current restrictiveness broadly appropriate
squawks.detail: Lombardelli and Pill see a case for another hike in the near term, with Pill reported as saying one 25bp rise is unlikely to be enough, and Greene says more hikes will likely be needed. Lombardelli says the price effects of the energy shock are larger and more persistent, Mann says second-order effects are now more robust, and Governor Bailey says part of the rise in the market curve reflects risk premia rather than expected rates.

squawks.headline: BoE changes its guidance and will now assess the evidence at each meeting, adjusting Bank Rate as necessary
squawks.detail: The Bank says most members judged policy to be still restrictive and that stronger than expected activity data added to the case for tightening. It says the risk of second-round effects has risen since September, though evidence of them from higher energy prices remains limited, and members still disagree on how much slack there is in the economy.

squawks.headline: Bank of England raises Bank Rate to 4.0% from 3.75%, in line with forecasts
squawks.detail: The consensus forecast was 4.0%.

squawks.headline: Iraq's government is reported to be closing several of its border crossings with Iran
squawks.detail: Reports say the Iraqi government has announced that it is closing several border crossings with Iran. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: European Commission pays €4.36bn to Ukraine from its €90bn support loan
squawks.detail: European Commission President von der Leyen announced the €4.36bn payment as Ukraine goes into its fifth winter of the war. She said EU support will continue alongside efforts to reach a peace settlement.

squawks.headline: US Challenger job cuts come in at 43.994K, up from 43.281K
squawks.detail: The Challenger report puts announced US layoffs at 43.994K, compared with 43.281K in the previous reading. No forecast was given.

squawks.headline: Italy is set to approve reimbursements for gas-fired power plants to bring down electricity costs
squawks.detail: A newswire headline reports that the Italian government is preparing to approve the reimbursement measure for gas plants to reduce power costs. No figures were given.

squawks.headline: ECB's Zigman sees a fairly high likelihood of a rate rise in December but says the extent of further tightening is still unclear
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Zigman said there is a sizeable chance that rates are raised in December. He added that it is too early to judge how much more tightening will be needed.

squawks.headline: Oman and Iran foreign ministers call for moving beyond de-escalation towards lasting agreements
squawks.detail: Oman's state news agency ONA reports the two foreign ministers held a phone call. They discussed arrangements to secure sea routes and keep trade and energy flowing, and stressed a shift from de-escalation to durable deals.

squawks.headline: Oman and Iran foreign ministers discuss securing sea routes and keeping trade and energy flowing
squawks.detail: Oman's state news agency ONA reported the foreign ministers said the focus should move from de-escalation to lasting agreements. They also discussed measures to keep trade and energy flowing.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says military action in Ukraine will go on because peace efforts have stalled, though Russia still wants a peaceful outcome
squawks.detail: The Kremlin said Russia would protect its interests either militarily or through peace, if Kyiv shows political will. It added that safeguarding Russia's interests cannot depend on events in the United States after the US elections.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says Russian diesel will find buyers as tankers change course, declining to discuss commercial matters
squawks.detail: The Kremlin said Russian diesel will find buyers when asked about tankers carrying it changing course, and said it could not discuss commercial issues. The remarks follow reports that the US diesel deal with Russia is faltering.

squawks.headline: Eurozone producer prices rise 11.1% y/y in September, above the 10.6% forecast, up from 8.2%
squawks.detail: Eurozone PPI for September rose 11.1% year on year, against a forecast of 10.6% and 8.2% previously. The monthly rise was 2.5%, in line with forecasts.

squawks.headline: Eurozone producer prices rise 2.5% m/m, matching forecast, after a 1.9% increase
squawks.detail: Eurozone PPI rose 2.5% month on month, in line with the 2.5% forecast and up from 1.9% previously.

squawks.headline: Japan's PM Takaichi tells Macron that Japan has grave concern over the EU's proposed Industrial Accelerator Act
squawks.detail: Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi raised Japan's concern about the EU's proposed Industrial Accelerator Act in a teleconference with French President Macron. She asked France to respond appropriately.

squawks.headline: RBA official warns public confidence in the bank's ability to control inflation is slipping
squawks.detail: A senior Reserve Bank of Australia official said on Thursday that public trust in the RBA's inflation fight is eroding, and that losing it could make bringing down inflation more costly, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: Bank of Korea and South Korean government to buy at least tens of billions of dollars of US Treasuries, Korean media report
squawks.detail: Korean media report that the purchases are meant to significantly increase South Korea's foreign exchange reserves, currently $443.1 billion. The total is expected to be at least tens of billions of dollars.

squawks.headline: Sterling heads for a seventh straight daily gain against a weaker dollar before the Bank of England decision
squawks.detail: Reuters says sterling is on course for its seventh consecutive daily rise against the dollar. Investors are holding back ahead of the Bank of England policy announcement later on Thursday.

squawks.headline: UK construction PMI drops to 43.6 in October, well below the 46.5 forecast, from 46.1
squawks.detail: The UK construction PMI came in at 43.6, against a forecast of 46.5 and a previous reading of 46.1. It was released ahead of today's Bank of England decision.

squawks.headline: Saudi Arabia issues civil defence alerts warning of potential danger in Yanbu
squawks.detail: Saudi authorities warned of potential danger in Yanbu, and the Saudi civil defence said it had issued alerts there. No further details were given and no market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: South Korea is reported to be considering purchases of long-dated US Treasuries
squawks.detail: A market news account reports that South Korea is weighing buying long-term US government debt. No size or timing was given.

squawks.headline: Italian retail sales rise 0.1% m/m, slightly above the 0.05% forecast, after a 0.3% gain
squawks.detail: On a non-seasonally adjusted basis, Italian retail sales grew 1.6% year on year, up from 0.5% the month before.

squawks.headline: Norges Bank holds its key policy rate at 4.5%, in line with forecasts
squawks.detail: Norway's central bank kept its key policy rate at 4.5%, matching the forecast and the previous setting. The decision came ahead of the Bank of England's announcement later today.

squawks.headline: German Chamber of Commerce raises 2026 German GDP growth forecast to 1% from 0.3%, and sees 1% growth in 2027
squawks.detail: The German Chamber of Commerce now forecasts German GDP growth of 1% in 2026, up from its previous 0.3%. It forecasts growth of 1% for 2027.

squawks.headline: ECB's Moulin says French budget uncertainty is adding to the rise in bond yields and France must adopt a budget by year-end
squawks.detail: ECB official Moulin said higher yields are a new test for the financial sector and could weigh on the economy. He said it is essential for France to adopt a budget by the end of the year.

squawks.headline: ECB's Schnabel says getting public finances back to a sustainable level has become harder; ECB will slowly build a long-term bond portfolio
squawks.detail: ECB Executive Board member Schnabel also said the ECB will build a long-term securities portfolio slowly once its legacy holdings have run down enough. She added that banks should again be able to use central bank loans without stigma.

squawks.headline: ECB's Schnabel warns non-bank finance growth and higher public debt could threaten monetary dominance
squawks.detail: ECB Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel said the rise of non-bank finance and increased public debt could threaten monetary dominance. She also said returning public finances to a sustainable path has become harder.

squawks.headline: Swiss unemployment rate holds at 3.1% seasonally adjusted in October, in line with forecast
squawks.detail: The seasonally adjusted Swiss unemployment rate was 3.1%, matching both the forecast and the previous reading. The unadjusted rate was unchanged at 3.0%, also in line with forecast.

squawks.headline: China says buying more US farm goods depends on both sides putting reciprocal tariff cuts into effect
squawks.detail: On Thursday China's Commerce Ministry said it is open to buying more US agricultural products, but only once both sides finalise and carry out reciprocal tariff cuts on $60 billion of goods each way.

squawks.headline: French industrial production falls 0.5% m/m, missing the 0.3% rise forecast, after a 0.3% drop
squawks.detail: France's industrial production fell 0.5% month on month. The forecast was for a 0.3% rise, and the previous month showed a 0.3% fall.

squawks.headline: RBA Deputy Governor Hauser says consumption growth has been stronger than expected
squawks.detail: RBA Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said consumer spending growth has held up better than the bank anticipated. He also said the bank had not tried to steer market expectations through open-mouth operations.

squawks.headline: Oil holds on to its losses in early trading and is down almost a fifth this week
squawks.detail: The FT reported that oil prices held their losses on Thursday morning, leaving them down almost a fifth over the week, ahead of today's Bank of England decision.

squawks.headline: RBA Deputy Governor Hauser says inflation is too high on every measure
squawks.detail: Reserve Bank of Australia Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said inflation is too high whichever measure is used. The remark follows his earlier comments on the board's last meeting.

squawks.headline: SNB chairman Schlegel says early signs point to the Swiss economy still growing
squawks.detail: Swiss National Bank chairman Schlegel said initial indications are that the Swiss economy continues to grow, according to remarks reported by HZ.

squawks.headline: RBA Deputy Governor Hauser says the board had very lively debates at its last meeting and members were not cornered
squawks.detail: Reserve Bank of Australia Deputy Governor Hauser described the board as diverse, with very lively discussion at the last meeting. He rejected the view that board members are being driven into a corner at meetings.

squawks.headline: SNB chairman Schlegel says no significant second-round inflation effects have been seen so far
squawks.detail: Swiss National Bank chairman Martin Schlegel said significant second-round effects have not yet appeared. He also said the SNB would step in if price stability were threatened.

squawks.headline: Swedish CPIF inflation slows to 1.1% y/y in October, below the 1.4% forecast; CPI eases to 0.9%
squawks.detail: Statistics Sweden data show CPIF inflation down from 1.5%, against a 1.4% forecast, and flat on the month against an expected 0.3% rise. Headline CPI fell to 0.9% from 1.1% (forecast 1.2%), and CPIF excluding energy slowed to 0.1% y/y from 0.5%, with a 0.2% fall on the month.

squawks.headline: German industrial orders rise 4.4% m/m, just short of the 4.5% forecast, after a 10.6% fall
squawks.detail: German industrial orders rose 4.4% month on month, against a forecast of 4.5%. The previous reading was a fall of 10.6%.

squawks.headline: Sterling slips against the yen ahead of today's Bank of England decision
squawks.detail: FXStreet reports that sterling is weaker against the yen in early trading before the Bank of England's policy announcement. No figures were given.

squawks.headline: Russia steps up military support for Iran with a missile launcher deal, FT reports
squawks.detail: The FT reports that Moscow has increased its military aid to Tehran, including a deal on missile launchers, even though the Ukraine war is putting strain on its resources.

squawks.headline: FT survey of economists puts UK inflation peak at 4.4% in 2027, with typical energy bills up nearly £470 in January
squawks.detail: An FT survey of economists shows UK inflation peaking at 4.4% in 2027. The FT also reports that typical household energy bills are expected to rise by nearly £470 in January, to about £2,200 a year.

squawks.headline: Dollar index falls 0.26% to 101.21 in Asian trading, and the euro gains 0.25% to $1.1257
squawks.detail: The dollar extended its losses in Asian hours on Thursday as oil and chip stocks came under pressure following the US midterm results. The euro rose 0.25% to $1.1257 and the New Zealand dollar gained 0.60% to $0.5656.

squawks.headline: Bank of Thailand governor says 2% growth is below a sustainable pace and growth may slow in early 2027
squawks.detail: Thailand's central bank chief said economic growth of 2% is not enough to be sustainable. He added that growth may ease in early 2027.

squawks.headline: Sterling edges higher above 1.3450 against the dollar ahead of today's Bank of England decision
squawks.detail: Sterling posted modest gains in Asian trading and was holding above 1.3450 against the dollar before the Bank of England's rate announcement due later today.

squawks.headline: US Treasuries firm and the dollar weakens as lower oil prices ease inflation concerns; US 10-year yield at 4.88%
squawks.detail: A market wrap reports that falling oil prices after the US midterms supported Treasuries and weighed on the dollar, with the US 10-year yield at 4.88% in early Asian trading.

squawks.headline: 20-year JGB yield falls 2bp to 3.64% as long-dated Japanese yields retreat after the drop in oil
squawks.detail: Long-dated Japanese government bond yields fell after the drop in oil prices, according to the WSJ. Asia-Pacific equities opened mostly higher after the US rally, while Treasury yields and oil moved lower.

squawks.headline: BoJ September minutes show members agreed the bank should keep raising its policy rate and reducing monetary easing
squawks.detail: Minutes of the Bank of Japan's September meeting show one member favoured moving the policy rate closer to its target relatively soon, and another said hikes would need to speed up if prices showed signs of deviating upward. Many members said rising crude oil prices kept upside risks to prices high, and several noted underlying CPI inflation had been close to 2% lately.

squawks.headline: White House sets 14 December hearing on mortgage fraud allegations against Fed Governor Cook, NYT reports
squawks.detail: Citing an unnamed White House official, the New York Times reported that the hearing is a new step in President Trump's effort to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook.

squawks.headline: SNB chairman Schlegel says the SNB will not hesitate to change policy if price stability is at risk
squawks.detail: Swiss National Bank chairman Schlegel said Swiss inflation rose, with the October figure above expectations. He said there have been no major second-round effects so far but they cannot be ruled out later, and the SNB will watch them closely.

squawks.headline: US stocks and bonds rally after the midterm elections while oil prices fall
squawks.detail: A US market wrap reports US equities and bonds both gaining after the midterm election results as oil prices slid. No yield figures were given.

squawks.headline: Trump rules out scaling back his tariffs after the midterms, citing 3,000 plants under construction
squawks.detail: In a CNBC interview, US President Trump said he would not pare back his tariffs, arguing that removing them would halt building at 3,000 plants now under construction. He also said he could work with Democrats on financial ideas, but declined to comment on a cap on credit card rates.

squawks.headline: Trump's diesel deal with Russia is faltering as US fuel supplies hit a 20-year low, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the Trump administration's diesel arrangement with Russia is stalling while US fuel supplies are at their lowest in 20 years.

squawks.headline: Brent crude futures settle at their lowest level since 31 August
squawks.detail: Brent futures settled at their lowest since 31 August, after the day's 8.67% fall to $94.62 a barrel.

squawks.headline: Brent crude futures settle 8.67% lower at $94.62 a barrel, down $8.98
squawks.detail: Brent crude futures closed the session at $94.62 a barrel after an $8.98 fall, or 8.67%. Earlier in the day, WTI settled 8.29% lower at $88.12.

squawks.headline: WTI crude futures settle 8.29% lower at $88.12 a barrel, down $7.97
squawks.detail: December NYMEX WTI crude futures settled at $88.12 a barrel, down $7.97 or 8.29% on the day. December gasoline futures settled at $2.7286 a gallon and diesel at $4.2055 a gallon.

squawks.headline: ECB's Moulin says banks can cope with higher rates and the bank-sovereign loop risk has gone
squawks.detail: ECB policymaker Moulin said banks are able to handle rising rates, that a doom loop between banks and sovereigns is no longer a risk, and that France must solve its financial problems itself rather than rely on Frankfurt. He also said he is sceptical of the French government's plan to raise the cap on regulated savings.

squawks.headline: US Treasury accepts $6B in debt buyback after receiving $39.636B of offers
squawks.detail: The US Treasury accepted 7 of 40 eligible issues in a buyback targeting coupon securities maturing from 2037 to 2046, against $39.636B of offers.

squawks.headline: ECB's Kazaks says rates may rise gradually and need to go up if inflation risks spread
squawks.detail: ECB Governing Council member Kazaks said there could be a gradual increase in interest rates, and that rates would need to rise if inflation risks spread.

squawks.headline: US Treasury Secretary Bessent pledges sanctions on anyone who keeps supporting the Iranian regime by land, sea or air
squawks.detail: US Treasury Secretary Bessent made the pledge in a post on X. It follows new US Treasury sanctions related to Iran announced earlier on 4 November.

squawks.headline: Arab diplomatic sources report significant progress in US-Iran negotiations, with the direction expected to be clearer on Friday
squawks.detail: Lebanese broadcaster Al-Jadeed cited Arab diplomatic sources on 4 November. The report has not been officially confirmed.

squawks.headline: Trump says he would not have changed anything on Iran and the war will end when he decides, but any end has to be right
squawks.detail: Speaking on 4 November, the US President said he had not promised the Iran war would end straight after the midterm elections. He said he would have done nothing differently on Iran.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US will keep up its Iran campaign and that it was worth the midterm cost, as Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon
squawks.detail: In unscheduled remarks at the White House, President Trump said the action against Iran had been necessary and would continue. He said the war was worth it because Iran could not be allowed a nuclear weapon, and that he would probably get along with the Democrats unless they set out to be destructive.

squawks.headline: Trump agrees the Republican midterm defeat was largely down to the Iran war
squawks.detail: US President Trump says it is largely true that the Republicans lost the midterm elections because of the Iran war. Earlier, Vice President Vance gave the same reason.

squawks.headline: China's Xi says the Gulf should not become an arena for great-power rivalry as Beijing steps up its Iran war diplomacy
squawks.detail: According to Semafor, Chinese President Xi made the remarks as China increases its diplomatic efforts in the Gulf over the Iran war.

squawks.headline: US Treasury sanctions 4 India-based individuals and 9 companies for supporting Iran's shadow fleet
squawks.detail: The US Treasury says the 4 individuals and 9 companies, all based in India, are being sanctioned for supporting Iran's shadow fleet. It is part of the Iran sanctions action announced earlier today, which also included a warning that falsely flagged vessels have no valid protection or insurance.

squawks.headline: US Treasury's OFAC warns industry about vessels that may be falsely flagged and names a Turkey-based firm in Iran sanctions
squawks.detail: As part of its latest Iran-related sanctions, the US Treasury designated Turkey-based Fugo Ground Services for supporting Iran's aviation sector. Its Office of Foreign Assets Control also issued a new alert to industry on the risks of dealing with vessels that may be falsely flagged.

squawks.headline: Brent crude slides 10% to near $93 a barrel, its lowest in two months
squawks.detail: Brent crude is reported down 10% at close to $93 a barrel, its lowest level in two months, as the oil sell-off extends through the session.

squawks.headline: OBR's David Miles names fiscal drag as one of three main causes of near-stagnant UK household income growth this decade
squawks.detail: David Miles of the Office for Budget Responsibility said frozen income tax thresholds, which pull more people into higher tax bands, are one of three main reasons that growth in UK households' disposable income is close to stagnant in the current decade, City A.M. reports.

squawks.headline: US Treasury advisory committee finds AI-linked corporate borrowing is not crowding out demand for Treasuries
squawks.detail: The Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee reached this view at its latest meeting, Reuters reports. The committee also cautioned that the AI financing boom is still at an early stage.

squawks.headline: US Treasury announces new sanctions related to Iran
squawks.detail: The US Treasury Department posted new Iran-related sanctions on its website. No further details were given in the report.

squawks.headline: House Democratic leader Jeffries says Democrats will pass a bill to stop Trump's tariffs and end the Iran war
squawks.detail: House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries made the pledge after the Democrats won control of Congress in the midterms. He also said he had not heard from Trump.

squawks.headline: Brent crude falls to $95 a barrel, down 10% from Friday
squawks.detail: An economist reports that Brent crude is at $95 a barrel, 10% lower than on Friday, as the slide following the US midterm results continues.

squawks.headline: Brent crude futures extend their slide to more than $7 a barrel; US crude falls more than $5 to near $90
squawks.detail: Market reports show Brent crude futures down by more than $7 a barrel and US crude futures down by more than $5 a barrel. US crude is reported trading near $90 a barrel as the oil sell-off deepens.

squawks.headline: European gas prices fall by as much as 5.3% to €86.74/MWh
squawks.detail: European gas prices fell by as much as 5.3% to €86.74 per megawatt hour on Wednesday, according to a market report.
